subject: Access controls for customer data - RBAC & support access follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Cc: David Kim <david@redwood.ai>, Ethan Park <ethan@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 07 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Access controls for customer data - follow-up and next steps

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great to learn more about FinTrust's use cases and the sensitivity around customer PII and transaction data. Per our call, I wanted to recap the access-control items we discussed and propose concrete next steps so your security & procurement teams can review.

Summary of what we covered:
- RBAC model: role-based permissions (Admin, Developer, Read-Only, Support) with resource-scoped grants
- Support access: short-lived, auditable elevation for root-cause debugging; requires justification and approval
- Break-glass: emergency access that triggers multi-party notification and enhanced logging
- Audit & logging: immutable audit trail for ACL changes and elevated sessions; exportable to SIEM
- Data residency & retention: tenant data stays in your chosen region; retention configurable per workspace

Attachments: RBAC-overview.pdf (high-level roles + sample permission matrix)

Requested next steps:
1) Can you confirm who from FinTrust will own the security questionnaire (security@fintrust or procurement)?
2) Would your team like a short tech deep-dive (30-45 min) on support access and break-glass flows? Ethan (cc'd) can lead this.
3) I can send a short write-up of the proposed break-glass policy and sample audit screenshots — is that useful for procurement?

If that sounds good, I can schedule the follow-up for next week.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Hi Lauren — thanks for the questions. Below are more concrete answers that you can pass to procurement/security. Happy to convert into a one-pager.

Support access (requested elevations)
- Who can request: Redwood support or your FinTrust admins can request a support session. Each request must include a short justification (ticket id / incident link).
- Approval flow: by default, requests are auto-queued to the on-call owner for the workspace. For production-critical tenants we recommend an approval gate (one or two approvers) — this can be enforced in the console.
- Session duration: default TTL is 30 mins for elevated credentials; sessions can be extended with additional approval. All sessions require the requester to state purpose and are logged.

Break-glass procedures
- Triggers: human request (operator), automated alert (monitoring), or on-call escalation.
- Authorization model: emergency access can be configured to require two-person approval (manager + security) or allow immediate single-person break-glass depending on your policy. We recommend two-person for high-risk ops.
- Safeguards: break-glass actions are time-limited, constrained to specific resources, and require a free-text justification that is recorded in the audit log.

Auditing & log access
- What we record: all ACL changes, elevated sessions (start/end, actor, justification), API keys issued, and resource-level access events.
- Exports/integrations: logs are available via our audit-logs API (JSON) and we provide push integrations to Splunk/Datadog via secure outbound collectors. Exports for e-discovery are available as gzipped JSON or CSV.
- Retention: audit logs retention configurable per contract — standard 90 days; enterprise plans support 1-7 years.

Attachments I'm sending: BreakGlass-proc.docx (one-page break-glass summary), RBAC-overview.pdf. Also linking our docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/access-controls.
